summary: The limits and dates match Cloudflare's pages as read today: 100,000 requests and 10 ms, R2's 10 GB with no egress, D1, KV and Durable Objects, 10,000 neurons and 71 Cloudflare-hosted models, Browser Run renamed on 15 April, temporary accounts on 19 June, Python Workers GA on 21 September, cf on 28 September, AI Search billing on 1 November with 5 million tokens and 1,000 queries of each kind, Agent Lee's limits, and the Worker is 83 lines. Fix first the Wrangler timeline: the 18 months of maintenance start when the cf beta ends, not now.

facts.notes: Checked on 18 October 2026 against the pages the article links: Workers limits and pricing (100,000 requests a day, 10 ms CPU, $5 for 10 million requests, up to 5 minutes CPU configurable on paid, 5 cron triggers free, static assets free and unlimited); R2 pricing (10 GB, 1 million Class A, 10 million Class B, no egress) and data location (EU, US, FedRAMP jurisdictions); D1 (5 GB, 5 million rows read, 100,000 written a day); KV (100,000 reads, 1,000 writes a day); Durable Objects (100,000 requests a day, 5 GB, SQLite only on free); Queues 10,000 operations and Workflows 3,000 steps a day; Workers AI pricing (10,000 neurons a day, $0.011 per 1,000) and catalogue ("We found 71 models", all tagged Cloudflare-hosted, every family named is present); privacy page sentence (verbatim); Email Service pricing (paid plan only, 3,000 a month, $0.35 per 1,000); Browser Run limits (10 minutes a day; renamed 15 April 2026 per the changelog); Deploy buttons (Workers only); temporary accounts changelog (19 June 2026, 60 minutes); cf post (28 September 2026, open beta, 18 months of maintenance after the beta ends); Python Workers GA (21 September 2026); Agent Lee docs (beta, DNS changes with approval, cannot deploy applications or Workers); AI Search free allowance (5 million ingestion tokens, 1,000 queries of each kind, billing 1 November 2026, via ppc.land as the Cloudflare pricing URL I tried returned 404); Access free to 50 users (third-party pricing pages only); sgit-ai in this environment is v0.21.0. The Worker code block is 83 lines. Not checked: the Email Sending beta date, the Workers AI and AI Gateway path to other providers' models, the 39-file test vault, and that the hosted sgit server lacks CORS preflight (tested from the author's machine).

voice.notes: First person, the want stated plainly, what does not work said plainly. No superlatives, no em-dashes. "Claude Code" is named as a product in the setup section; I read the house rule on model names as being about which model wrote the article, so I have not raised it as a finding.

claims.notes: Tested, prototype and not-yet-run-on-a-real-account are separated in the vault section, the limits and the sources; the limits name the real gaps (large files, one token, no rate limits).

conversions.notes: No currency or unit conversions; 83 lines is the same in the title, summary, In short, caption and body; the free limits in the figure caption match the blocks list.

health.notes: All Cloudflare links load (the AI Search pricing page is not linked, which is just as well, as the URL I tried is 404); figures exist; graph quotes appear verbatim; no stale section summary.

people.notes: No private person, no key; the Worker's optional ACCESS_TOKEN is a placeholder name, not a value.

findings.quote: will replace Wrangler over the next 18 months
findings.issue: Cloudflare's post says maintenance support for Wrangler continues for 18 months after the cf open beta ends, with a final major Wrangler release at that point; the 18 months have not started. The same slip is in What I would watch ("Wrangler is maintained for 18 months").
findings.suggestion: "will replace Wrangler, which stays maintained for 18 months after the cf beta ends".

findings.quote: The vault API sgit talks to has seven endpoints: info, read, list, batch, write, delete and destroy.
findings.issue: The Worker shown also answers an eighth path, auth (returns ok), so the code serves eight routes, not seven.
findings.evidence: The article's own code block: `if (p[2] === 'auth') return J({ ok: true });`
findings.suggestion: Say "seven endpoints, plus an auth check that always answers ok", or drop the auth route if sgit does not need it.

findings.quote: all marked Cloudflare-hosted, running "on GPUs on Cloudflare's network"
findings.issue: The quoted phrase is on the Workers AI overview page (developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/), which is not among the sources; neither the models catalogue nor the privacy page, which are linked, carries it.
findings.evidence: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/ ("models running on GPUs on Cloudflare's network"); the models and privacy pages, all read 18 October 2026
findings.suggestion: Add the Workers AI overview page to the sources, or attribute the phrase to it.

findings.quote: In beta since April, on the paid plan
findings.issue: The linked Email Service pricing page gives the plan, the 3,000 emails and the $0.35, but says nothing about a beta or a start date; I found the April date only on third-party comparison pages.
findings.suggestion: Link the Cloudflare announcement that dates the beta, or drop "since April".
